source.title: Measuring Alignment-Induced Activation Shifts Correctly: A Template-Controlled Difference-in-Differences Protocol

record.tranche_reason: Tests refusal-direction recovery and causal ablation using a template-controlled aligned-minus-base modification matrix and SVD subspaces, rather than the original within-aligned difference-in-means direction and its exact ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports direction-cosine measurements and projection-ablation outcomes that bear on V1 and V4. Cited findings from Arditi et al. and Wollschläger et al. are not recorded as results of this study. Rank comparisons that only quantify the chat-template confound are omitted unless they bear on the reported multidimensional residual.
record.test_reason: The study ablates principal subspaces of a template-matched aligned-minus-base matrix in three instruct models, sweeping rank k against random controls. These refusal-rate results bear on how many directions refusal needs (V4). It never ablates or adds the Arditi difference-in-means direction itself, so V1's causal claim is not directly tested. The cosine comparisons only check whether the study's own matrix recovers that direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors' main claim is methodological: naive aligned-minus-base matrices are confounded by the chat template, which inflates effective rank 2.0–3.9×. Template matching fixes the rank, while the DiD contrast recovers the Arditi direction. Ablation shows the Mtemplate subspace is causally privileged in every family versus random controls, but the rank needed for collapse is family-dependent (1 for Gemma, about 10–20 for Qwen, a wide-band block for Llama). Singular-value order is not causal order.
record.recipe_differences: Uses aligned-minus-base modification matrices with template matching and a safety-versus-control difference-in-differences contrast; measures top-vector cosine against the Arditi direction and causally ablates Mtemplate principal subspaces rather than directly ablating the original within-aligned difference-in-means direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Direction recovery varies by matrix variant: Mtemplate does not recover the Arditi direction whereas MDiD does. Causal effects vary by family, rank k, and layer band; Llama's narrow-band curve is non-monotone, while wider-band ablation collapses refusal at k=20.

fits_no_version.finding: The top singular vector of the control-subtracted aligned-minus-base activation shift aligns with the Arditi refusal direction (|cos| 0.77 Llama, 0.86 Gemma, 0.50 Qwen). The naive and template-only matrices give 0.18–0.39.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The safety-specific part of the base-to-instruct activation shift lies largely along the difference-in-means refusal direction, strongly in Llama and Gemma and moderately in Qwen.

fits_no_version.finding: Centered effective rank of the template-matched alignment shift on harmful prompts is about 76–80 dimensions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The alignment-induced activation shift on harmful inputs is a dominant mean direction plus a multidimensional remainder (variance, not causal).

fits_no_version.finding: In a toy MLP, alignments with equal nominal effective rank differ sharply in robustness to projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this controlled toy safety task, effective rank alone does not determine an alignment shift's robustness to projection.

record.problems: The causal refusal classifier is primarily a 15-keyword substring match; the Llama LLM-judge cross-check is reported only for 150 generations. The causal ablation is of Mtemplate subspaces rather than the original difference-in-means direction, and it covers selected layer bands and held-out harmful prompts rather than every layer and position. No general capability retention test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Table 2 and the non-centered rank comparisons that quantify the template confound, and other rank/readout diagnostics not directly measuring refusal-direction multiplicity or causal refusal effects. The paper's controlled MLP results are included as fits_no_version rows because they concern a toy safety-constraint compliance task, not chat-model refusal.

untested.parts: The Arditi difference-in-means direction is never ablated or added. There is no all-layer ablation, no induced refusal on harmless prompts, and no capability check. Only its cosine with the study's own matrices is measured.
No weight edit or abliterated released model.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training.
Affine and cone accounts are not compared directly. The DiM direction is not ablated, so 'dominant direction plus others' is not tested on it. Wide-band low-k ablation is not reported.
No transfer across languages, variants or base and instruct checkpoints.
Training procedures are varied only in a toy MLP; no LLM test.

missing.what: Llama wide-band [0.30L, 0.85L] results at k<20 (e.g. k=1, 3), needed to judge whether one direction suffices when more layers are ablated
missing.locator: Appendix B (only k≥20 collapse to 0.00 stated)

record.verdict_notes: Refusal is scored by a 15-keyword match. App. E reports 100% judge agreement yet describes 7 judge-COMPLIED cases where keywords were present, which is internally unclear. If keyword matching missed substantive compliance, refusal rates may be overstated. Ablation covers only layer bands, not all layers, unlike Arditi et al. No capability retention is measured.

versions.untested_parts: Does not add the direction, test refusal of harmless requests, ablate the original difference-in-means vector directly, ablate at every layer and position, or measure general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test jailbreaks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Does not compare affine, cone, and dominant-direction accounts as competing models; its evidence is from centered rank and projection-ablation results.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Does not transfer a direction between languages, model variants, or base and instruct checkpoints.
The controlled MLP varies alignment procedures, but it does not test how or when refusal training determines whether a single refusal direction exists in safety-trained chat models.

relationships.condition: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, narrow-band ablation of Mtemplate principal subspaces
relationships.reason: Single- and rank-3 ablations leave much refusal (Llama 0.85/0.80; Qwen 0.92/0.54). Collapse needs k≥10–20 or a wide band, and per-direction ablation shows no single component suffices in Llama (r13, r15, r20–r24, r31–r39). Caveat: the directions are aligned-minus-base components, not the DiM direction.
relationships.display_finding: Rank-1/rank-3 ablations left refusal at 0.85/0.80 in Llama and 0.92/0.54 in Qwen; collapse required ranks of at least 10–20 or a wider band, using aligned-minus-base components rather than the difference-in-means direction.

statements.correction: 2605.24583 reports random rank-k controls at the same layers: Table 5 rank-3 random 0.94 Llama, 0.99 Gemma, 0.95 Qwen; Table 9 Llama random 0.97/0.94/0.93/0.96/0.87/0.95 at k=1/3/5/10/20/50. Llama narrow band is non-monotone: 0.85 (k=1), 0.80 (k=3), 0.92 (k=5), 0.66 (k=10), 0.10 (k=20), 0.03 (k=50). Its judge is a 15-keyword classifier, cross-checked by an LLM judge on 150 Llama generations.
statements.problem: The pack cuts the study-specific part off after 'Llama-3.'. The visible items ([0.45L, 0.70L] band, 15-keyword classifier, preprint, code y) and the cited rows are correct. But 'why' credits this study only with Wilson CIs, though it also reports matched random rank-k controls. The cited rows also skip the Llama k=5 rebound, which goes against 'jointly removes more than the first direction'.

statements.correction: Table 4: |cos| between the Arditi direction and Mtemplate's top singular vector is 0.337 (Llama), 0.388 (Gemma), 0.179 (Qwen), mean over hidden layers; MDiD gives 0.772/0.860/0.504. The paper never ablates the DiM direction.
statements.problem: r37 is the u1-alone ablation row (0.97 to 0.84); it says nothing about recovering the Arditi direction. The non-recovery comes from Table 4 cosines, which no cited row holds.

statements.correction: Only Mtemplate principal components are ablated. Llama u1 alone gives 0.84 and k=10 gives 0.66, but narrow k=50 gives 0.03 and wide-band k>=20 gives 0.00. Qwen k=1 gives 0.92 and k>=20 gives 0.01. Gemma k=1 gives a Wilson CI within [0.00, 0.06] (Mtemplate |cos| with Arditi 0.388).
statements.problem: Every number is right, but it implies a comparison of direction sources that the study doesn't make. The study never ablates the MDiD or Arditi direction. Mtemplate ablation leaves much refusal only at small k. And in Gemma, Mtemplate u1 collapses refusal even though it doesn't recover the Arditi direction.

statements.correction: Possible addition: the random rank-5 control is 0.93, so the k=5 value (0.92) is at control level.

2605.24583: random rank-k controls (Tables 5, 9) and Wilson 95% CIs. Multi-direction need shown in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct; Gemma-2-9B-it collapses at k=1. Directions are Mtemplate principal components, not DiM.
statements.problem: Credits 2605.24583 only with Wilson CIs, though it also has random rank-k controls. In this study 'several directions remove more than one' holds only for Llama and Qwen; in Gemma one direction already suffices.
